To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
30% of IgA deficient serum samples were positive in at least one of three βhCG tests.

30% of 54 Ig A deficient patient sera yielded false positive pregnancy tests by 3 different beta human chorionic gondotropin (hCG) assays and 39% of patient sera contained significant levels of heterophile antibody.
30% of the IgA deficient sera yielded positive pregnancy test by one or more βhCG assays.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel method to identify and quantify the amount of βHCG in human blood serum.
the detection of heterophile antibodies in the sera of immunoglobulin A deficient patients.
the frequency of false positives for beta hCG in IgA deficiency.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the frequency of false positives in the three assays was 30% (16/54) in the IgA deficient patients, and that this is a significant number.
the false positive βhcg tests are due to anti‐goat antibodies, and that the false positive pregnancy tests are due to heterophile antibodies.
false positive pregnancy tests are common in IgG deficient patients and that the possibility of a false positive test should be considered prior invasive procedures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IgA deficient sera may have heterophile antibody activity, and this may cause false positive pregnancy tests.
IgA deficiency is associated with the presence of heterophil antibodies.
IgA deficient patients have high levels of heterophile antibody and these antibodies are capable of interfering with βHCG assays.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IgA deficiency is a common cause of heterophile antibodies.
false positive βhCH tests in IgA deficient patient serum are common and may lead to unnecessary procedures and medical care.
IgA deficient patients can have false positive pregnancy tests due to heterophile antibodies.
